eps.o: Muldoon inspects the raptor pen and realizes the animals are deliberately probing the electric fence for weaknesses, immediately establishing how smart and dangerous the pack is.
A routine feeding turns into a bad sign that the raptor situation is not actually under control, with clues that the pack may be larger or less contained than expected.
While dealing with the tyrannosaur paddock, Muldoon makes an “impossible discovery” that threatens the basic viability of the park and expands the danger beyond the raptors alone.
Muldoon watches the adult rex hunt, then encounters a juvenile tyrannosaur, proving there is more than one massive predator problem on the island.
After a juvenile tyrannosaur captures a young raptor, Muldoon gets dragged into another ugly containment situation that links the rex subplot back to the raptor crisis.
Trouble in the dilophosaur enclosure reveals a larger, nastier, more novel-inspired version of the species and shows that the park’s other attractions are every bit as unstable as the raptor paddock.
Muldoon spots an intruder inside the dilophosaur enclosure and has to respond fast, shifting from cautious observation to outright lethal action
Just when Muldoon thinks the threat has been neutralized, the Big One proves otherwise and the possibility of a real escape becomes much more immediate.
Muldoon finds an eggshell, starts asking hard questions about breeding and control, and also has to prepare for a new animal arriving at the park.
A supposedly contained velociraptor emergency turns into a direct attack, pushing Muldoon into a time-sensitive fight to keep the situation from spiraling.
Muldoon returns to the raptor pen and finds the feeding gate open, meaning one of the raptors is out and containment is starting to fail in the worst possible way.

This entry appears to widen the tyrannosaur storyline into breeding and backstory territory, tying the rex arc more directly into the park’s broader instability. Public descriptions for this one are thinner, so this summary is more title-driven than the others.
Muldoon has to rescue a worker stranded on scaffolding inside the aviary while aggressive, territorial flyers turn the whole thing into a survival sequence.
During a storm, Muldoon restores some power in the aviary only to discover a dead workman, the smell of decay, and a velociraptor waiting in the electrical room.

In the aftermath of a storm, Muldoon finds dinosaurs crossing into the wrong paddocks and discovers a metriacanthosaurus feeding on a dead sauropod, signaling that containment on Isla Nublar is breaking down fast.
Muldoon’s investigation into damaged containment leads to a closer look at the Metriacanthosaurs and their matriarch, Mary, as Jurassic Park’s growing instability becomes impossible to ignore.
When Robbie ends up in serious trouble, Muldoon is pulled into yet another fast-moving containment crisis, forcing him to act before the situation turns fatal.

Muldoon learns that another Jurassic Park worker has died, and this time Hammond himself is trying to keep the details controlled. As Muldoon reviews the incident, the footage points to another serious failure inside the park’s safety systems and shows how quickly InGen’s official story falls apart.
The park receives its first Baryonyx. During transport, the situation quickly turns dangerous when the animal’s container is compromised, forcing Muldoon to respond before things get worse.
Muldoon investigates a disturbing incident involving Jurassic Park’s newly introduced Baryonyx and an unfortunate gatekeeper, exposing the dangers of handling the park’s unpredictable predators.

A mysterious subject on Isla Sorna becomes the focus of a dangerous encounter, Muldoon is investigating further showing once again that InGen’s “Site B” still hides threats that are never fully understood or controlled.

A secret nest discovery forces careful choices, a distressed Styracosaurus shows unusual fear, and an old piece of equipment turns up where it shouldn’t—raising new questions about what’s really moving through the park.

Muldoon, Harding, Robbie and Skylar operate independently after park management continues to ignore the growing threat. They check the Styracaceous barn, observe a Pachycephalosaurs and begin to investigate a fence tool found inside the barn.

Muldoon and head Gerry review suspicious trail-cam footage from the recent Styracosaurus inspection. Meanwhile on Site B, behavioral specialist Tony discovers a critical breach involving a mated raptor pair.

Following the death of an escaped Velociraptor, Robert Muldoon continues investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. Meanwhile, daily operations at Jurassic Park carry on as he turns his attention to the Dilophosaurus enclosure, where even routine feeding procedures demand caution.
